# Zero out, not cancel out

Taking a zero pair off the board is called **Zero out**, though teachers have asked for "cancel out". Every algebra tiles source we checked calls the pair a zero pair, and most say the pair is removed (Didax's guide names the rule the Zero Principle, NCETM says zero pairs "can be identified and removed as their value is zero"); none uses "zero out", but it keeps the zero in view. "Cancel" appears only as a casual gloss (Big Ideas Math, Math is Fun), and research-based sources warn against it: the Meadows Center (UT Austin) says "A zero pair is not simply 'canceling out,' but rather the addition of +1 and –1 to equal 0", and an NCTM 2023 talk (written up on MiddleWeb as "Stop using these four words in math class") notes that "cancel" is also used for combining like terms and dividing out common factors, which blurs them. "Remove zero pair" is the textbook phrase and a fair alternative if "Zero out" ever confuses students; don't switch to "cancel".
